chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: Movie stars, Lena Horne and chorus girls at the Cotton Club
summary: Crawford lists the stars who came in, says musicians could not mingle, and describes chorus girls invited to sit with patrons.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Now, did you -- at that time -- excuse me. At that time you say a lot of stars, a lot of movie stars and people came here?
Oh, yes, that was the place.
Do you remember some of the ones who
George Raft, Fred Astaire, oh, any of them that were big in that particular area of time.
You mean James Cagney --
When they were in New York, they had to stop in there. Cotton Club was the biggest club in New York City. (Inaudible) bar none, no question about it.
Did you get to know any of them well?
Herman Stocks and all that?
No, I mean of the stars who came in.
No.
Did -- were the band members allowed to talk with the patrons and stuff much in the Cotton Club?

Not too much. Do your job, go on back in your dressing room, dressing room. But those were big stars. You know, we didn't have that privilege, nobody. Maybe they'd call out a girl like Lena Horne to come sit with them or something like that. Well, that was all right, chorus girls and whatnot.
Oh, now did -- so now, was there -- so you mean a lot of the stars would have -- would invite people like --
Lena Horne.
And chorus girls to sit with them and talk.

Yes, but my wife was always the shy type, you know. She'd just sit back and twiddle her thumbs in the dressing room, make up, use some excuse, wipe it on -- putting on her face or taking one off. Of course, she's very nice looking. I think so. Yeah, they were -- let's see. Who's that girl? (Inaudible) big stars.
So like did they -- was -- was that -- so the guys would get interested in the chorus girls?
I don't know what they did after or what they did or anything. That's not my affair. I'm not interested in that. (Inaudible).
Oh, no, I wasn't so much -- I wasn't asking you whether or not you were interested. I was just trying to get a picture of what was --
Oh, we didn't --
-- what kind of things went on.

Those girls didn't want no musicians. Like the same girl told my wife -- they were pretty friendly -- then -- said, oh, you fooling with a musician? Better go get somebody (Inaudible) fooling with a musician, a drummer at that.
(Laughter)
